business.body: The Company is engaged in the business of trade show and exhibition booth solutions, offering both custom-built and modular exhibition options. Design and conceptualization are handled in-house and through project-based collaborations with professionals, while booth fabrication and related services are outsourced and carried out under the Company's supervision. outlook.body: The routed DRHP text discloses NO capacity, plant or capex expansion programme. The Fresh Issue objects are limited to (i) funding working capital requirements of the Company and (ii) general corporate purposes - there is no capex object, no new facility and no commissioning timeline. The Company's stated infrastructure model is deliberately asset-light: booth fabrication and related services are outsourced to subcontractors under Company supervision, the two godowns at Vasai/Virar (Maharashtra) and Madanayakanahally/Tumkur Road (Bengaluru, Karnataka) are rented and serve storage, logistics and fabrication support rather than owned manufacturing, and additional godown/storage space is rented temporarily at or near event sites as projects require. Geographic reach is described as already established rather than as a funded expansion plan - presence spanning India, Dubai, US, UK, Germany and other international regions, served through working relationships with local teams and a global network of sub-contractors; the accompanying disclosure shows international revenue rising from 0.61% of revenue from operations in FY23 to 12.83% for the period ended February 28, 2026, but the DRHP text provided states no forward target for it. The 'Our Business - Competitive Strengths' and business-strategy discussion referenced on page 195 is not included in the routed extract, so any expansion narrative contained there is not captured here.

business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Asset-light services model with a dual execution framework rather than owned manufacturing. Booth fabrication and related services are outsourced to subcontractors while design and conceptualization are handled in-house and through project-based collaborations; all subcontractors are directly hired and managed by the Company and all subcontracted work is carried out under its active guidance and on-ground supervision, with supervisors physically present on-site for the full duration of the project. Both partial and full subcontracting models are used, and the Company also takes on subcontracted work from other firms. The outsourcing model runs a formal two-step process (vendor screening - define project requirements, identify potential vendors, pre-screening checklist covering GST/PAN and financial stability, RFP/RFQ, proposal evaluation, vendor interviews, due diligence and background checks including litigation/blacklisting, final selection and contracting, onboarding and governance; then project execution - project management tools, milestone work plan, daily status calls and on-site monitoring, final delivery and handover). The in-house model covers material requirement definition (plywood, commercial ply, nylon carpet rolls and other construction/finish items), vendor shortlisting, RFQ, quotation evaluation, purchase order issue, material delivery and inspection, payment processing and inventory recordkeeping. Revenue by execution mode (% of total revenue): Subcontract 90.89% / 92.11% / 75.48% / 64.40% and In-house 9.11% / 7.89% / 24.52% / 35.60% for the period ended Feb 28, 2026 / FY25 / FY24 / FY23. Vendor and execution metrics (not cumulative), Feb 28, 2026 / FY25 / FY24 / FY23: total active subcontractors globally (domestic and international) 53 / 36 / 29 / 22; projects executed with international local allies 125 / 69 / 49 / 20; projects executed domestically 307 / 312 / 207 / 205; total booths delivered globally 432 / 381 / 256 / 225; total repeat clients 63 / 27 / 28 / 48; average project turnaround time 3 to 30 days in every period. The Company states it does not own fabrication machinery or permanent event spaces and instead rents godowns, fabrication equipment, raw materials and temporary project sites project-by-project; materials are sourced locally in overseas markets to reduce logistics dependencies. Risk factors disclose that there are no executed registered formal arrangements with the outsourced subcontractors governing specifications, quality standards, sales estimates or packaging, and that foreign outsourcing adds FX, cross-border regulatory, geopolitical and logistical exposure. Registered office and both godowns are on leasehold premises. International client base grew 245% over the last three years, from 20 to 69 international clients; total booths delivered globally grew at a stated CAGR of 30.13% from FY23 to FY25.

overview.business_model: The Company sells end-to-end exhibition booth services to corporate clients participating in trade fairs and expos: concept design and 3D visualization, project management, logistics, on-site supervision, fabrication, installation and post-event dismantling. Design and conceptualization are handled in-house and through project-based collaborations; booth fabrication and related services are outsourced to directly hired subcontractors working under the Company's guidance and on-ground supervision, under both partial and full subcontracting models. The Company also takes on subcontracted work from other firms. Revenue by execution method for the period ended February 28, 2026 was 90.89% subcontracted (Rs 5,436.02 lakhs) and 9.11% in-house (Rs 544.76 lakhs). Work is executed in India and, through local teams, in the United States, United Kingdom, Dubai, Germany, Spain and Singapore. Clients span Industrial Machinery & Equipment, Building Materials, Furnishing and Decor, Chemicals, Media & Entertainment, Healthcare and Cosmetics, and Food & Beverages.

compliance_legal.detail: Operations are exposed to fluctuations in global trade policies, particularly from the United States, which is the major export destination. Tariff escalation could reduce competitiveness of services in international markets and hit demand from downstream industries; retaliatory measures could restrict raw material availability, raise landed costs and strain domestic supply chains. Conditional exemptions, shifting quotas and unpredictable expansion of tariff coverage add regulatory uncertainty and may elevate procurement costs, impair pricing competitiveness, delay contract execution and restrict access to key export markets. The US 'Fair and Reciprocal Plan' has imposed tariffs across sectors including steel, aluminium, pharmaceuticals, textiles and electronics.

compliance_legal.detail: Form ADT-1 was not filed for the statutory auditor appointment made at the AGM of December 31, 2020; ADT-1 was subsequently filed in error treating the appointment as a casual vacancy for FY2021-22. verdict.our_read: An asset-light Mumbai exhibition-stand builder (Rs 5,980.78 lakhs 11M-FY26 revenue, 14.93% EBITDA margin, 90.89% of work subcontracted with no registered subcontractor agreements) whose thesis rides on funding working capital that swelled from Rs 91.53 to Rs 1,597.39 lakhs while it owns no fabrication capacity.

parameter_scores.basis: Revenue from operations Rs 2,591.09 (FY23) / 3,051.48 (FY24) / 5,151.82 (FY25) lakhs, with the 11-month stub to February 28, 2026 at Rs 5,980.78 lakhs already above the full FY25 year; booths delivered 225 to 432 and clients served 145 to 309 over the same span. Absolute scale is still small - FY25 revenue of Rs 5,151.82 lakhs against the single named listed peer's Rs 14,351.22 lakhs.

EBITDA margin 4.93% (FY23) to 9.67% (FY24) to 16.60% (FY25), then 14.93% in the 11-month stub; PAT margin 3.74% / 7.19% / 12.27% / 10.81%. Both margin lines stepped down in the stub period from the FY25 peak, and the model carries no owned capacity - fabrication materials and labour are 82.00% of total expenses in the stub against 91.32% in FY23.

RoNW 92.08% / 52.69% / 55.86% / 36.35% and ROE 170.64% / 84.14% / 81.67% / 44.42% across FY23 / FY24 / FY25 / stub. The levels reflect a very small equity base (net worth Rs 105.17 lakhs in FY23) that has since grown to Rs 1,778.30 lakhs, and the trend is downward as capital builds; RoCE is not printed in the routed sections.

CFO of Rs 25.42 (FY23), negative Rs 9.34 (FY24), Rs 14.01 (FY25) and Rs 225.17 lakhs (stub) against PAT of Rs 96.84 / 219.46 / 632.30 / 646.37 lakhs. FY2024 shows negative operating cash flow on PBT of Rs 294.62 lakhs with a Rs 256.42 lakh working-capital drag (Risk Factor 5). Restated PAT also diverges from PAT as per books in FY2024 (219.46 vs 223.93) and FY2023 (96.84 vs 93.54).

Net working capital requirement Rs 91.53 / 375.79 / 1,159.20 / 1,597.39 lakhs; trade receivables Rs 273.52 to Rs 911.22 lakhs; trade receivables turnover 18.46 to 13.63 to 13.22 to 7.89 times. Other Current Assets of Rs 1,187.71 lakhs is the largest current-asset block and includes a Rs 42.92 lakh 'Pre IPO Expenses' asset with no stated accounting policy. Debtor days are printed only to FY2025 (19 / 27 / 28) and not for the stub.

Total debt nil at February 28, 2026 (Rs 62.52 lakhs FY25, Rs 43.13 lakhs FY24, nil FY23); Debt-to-Equity 0.06 (FY2025), 0.10 (FY2024), 0.00 (FY2023); net worth Rs 1,778.30 lakhs and cash Rs 154.75 lakhs. Offsetting: the Rs 117.99 lakhs outstanding as at June 30, 2026 is entirely unsecured and recallable at any time (Risk Factor 21), the Rs 200.00 lakh Central Bank facility carries personal guarantees from both Promoters, and Note 26's borrowing-against-current-assets disclosure is internally contradictory as printed.

90.89% of stub-period revenue was executed through subcontractors (up from 64.40% in FY23) with no executed registered formal arrangements on specification, quality, sales estimates or packaging; no owned fabrication machinery, no plant, no capacity disclosure, net fixed assets Rs 38.37 lakhs; registered office and both godowns leasehold, the godowns on 11-month tenures expiring November 30 and December 31, 2026. Order lead times are short - purchase orders raised only a few weeks to 1-2 months before the event.

The RHP states it 'does not have any Group Company' while Propshop Worldwide Holdings Private Limited, controlled by both Promoters and in a similar line of business, is disclosed as an entity controlled by KMP with a non-compete signed (Risk Factor 32). Board of five with two Independent Directors, both appointed in March/April 2025; no Director has listed-company experience; board committee composition is absent from the routed extract.

Interest on delayed GST and TDS charged in ALL FOUR reported periods; RoC filing delays of up to 2,107 days (ADT-1 for first auditors), 528 days (INC-20A) and 7-14 days on four other forms; statutory auditors re-appointed for six years (April 01, 2022 to March 31, 2028) exceeding the five-year tenure under Section 139, corrected only by a Board resolution of July 23, 2025; PF return delays up to 196 days; FY2022-23 professional tax returns still pending; a GST ASMT-10 ITC-mismatch matter of Rs 24.06 lakhs now inside a Section 65 CGST audit with ADT-02 findings not yet issued.

The only object with a printed amount is working capital at Rs 1,662.00 lakhs (Rs 662.00 in FY2027 plus Rs 1,000.00 in FY2028), certified by HRJ & Associates on July 13, 2026; General Corporate Purposes is a placeholder capped at the lower of 15% of Gross Proceeds or Rs 1,000.00 lakhs. There is no capex, plant or machinery object and therefore no orders-not-placed exposure. Against that: estimates are unappraised, no monitoring agency is required as the Offer is under Rs 5,000 lakhs, no alternate funding source has been identified, and the funded amount covers only part of the projected FY2027-FY2028 working capital need.

Both Promoters sell in the Offer for Sale of up to 8,00,000 shares (5,00,000 and 3,00,000 respectively) and the Company receives no OFS proceeds, from a 94.55% pre-Offer holding; Minimum Promoters' Contribution of 20.02% of post-Offer capital is drawn entirely from the August 04, 2025 bonus issue at an acquisition price of Nil; weighted average cost of acquisition Rs 0.91 (primary) and Rs 0.82 (secondary). Promoters did fund the business through interest-free-looking loans that were fully repaid each period (Rs 319.00 lakhs received and repaid in FY23; Rs 63.01 lakhs in the stub) and provide personal guarantees on the Rs 200.00 lakh bank facility. No dividends have been paid in any past Financial Year.

Domestic revenue for the stub is printed as both Rs 5,213.73 and Rs 5,193.94 lakhs. The FY2023 weighted average share count of 95.41 lakh exceeds the year-end count of 0.10 lakh with no stated retrospective-adjustment explanation. The 'Share Application Money' caption carries the Shareholders' Funds subtotals (Rs 1,778.30 / 1,131.93 / 416.50 / 105.17 lakhs). Risk Factor 23 states insurance was obtained and, in the same paragraph, that no insurance is maintained; Risk Factor 53(h) refers to India's 'agrochemical industry' and Risk Factor 68 to an 'acquisition driven growth strategy', neither corroborated elsewhere.

Order book of Rs 1,356.86 lakhs as at June 30, 2026 (Rs 741.38 lakhs at February 28, 2026) against stub revenue of Rs 5,980.78 lakhs, with no unexecuted percentage, no execution timeline and no customer names disclosed. Purchase orders are typically raised only a few weeks to 1-2 months before the event; there are no firm-commitment long-term customer agreements (Risk Factor 9); average project turnaround 3 to 30 days; repeat clients moved 48 (FY23) / 28 (FY24) / 27 (FY25) / 63 (stub). The new corporate-event and exhibition-organisation vertical has two events (September and October 2025) and no separately disclosed revenue.

Not scoreable from this RHP. Price Band, floor price, cap price, Offer Price, aggregate Offer size, Net Proceeds, post-Offer paid-up capital, post-Offer promoter percentage and the issuer's own P/E are every one printed as placeholders, so no valuation multiple, dilution percentage or issue-size-to-earnings comparison can be stated. On the comparison side the RHP names exactly one identifiable listed peer (Exhicon Events Media Solutions Limited, P/E 27.31 computed on its BSE close of June 30, 2026 over FY2025 diluted EPS of Rs 15.56); the printed industry high, low and average of 27.31 are the same single company and are not an industry benchmark.

red_flags: Form ADT-1 for the first auditors' appointment (event dated September 10, 2019) was filed 2,107 days late, INC-20A 528 days late, and the statutory auditors were re-appointed at the September 30, 2022 AGM for six years - April 01, 2022 to March 31, 2028 - exceeding the five-year tenure permitted under Section 139 of the Companies Act, 2013, corrected only by taking the appointment on record up to March 31, 2027 by Board resolution of July 23, 2025 because the MCA V3 portal does not permit a revised ADT-1.

A Rs 104.46 lakh related-party 'Re-imbursement of Expense/ Purchase' to Whole-time Director Shreyas Rumade - roughly 6.5x his approved annual salary of Rs 15 lakh and the largest single non-loan related-party item in the table - with the period column attribution recorded as UNRESOLVED in the source.

The RHP states it 'does not have any Group Company as on the date of this Red Herring Prospectus' while simultaneously disclosing Propshop Worldwide Holdings Private Limited as an entity controlled by KMP, in a similar line of business, with both Promoters as directors and a non-compete agreement in place (Risk Factor 32); no financials for that entity appear anywhere and no transaction with it is reported in any of the four periods.

Interest on delayed payment of GST and of TDS was charged to Other Expenses in every one of the four reported periods (GST Rs 1.91 / 3.70 / 0.55 / 0.00 lakhs; TDS Rs 0.25 / 0.15 / 1.07 / 0.41 lakhs), a recurring rather than one-off pattern, corroborated by the cash-flow add-back 'Interest on statutory delay & W/off amount' of Rs 2.40 / 6.47 / 2.21 / 0.43 lakhs.

The bonus-issue arithmetic does not tie: 85,30,804 shares stated versus 85,30,909 implied by the stated 34:11 ratio on the Rs 276.00 lakh pre-bonus capital, and the post-bonus total of 1,12,90,804 shares is not divisible in the stated ratio; the WACA table dates the same event August 08, 2025 for 80,66,296 shares against August 04, 2025 for 85,30,804 elsewhere.

Note 26 'Borrowing against current assets' reads as printed that a loan was taken and a monthly current-asset return requirement exists, without stating whether those returns were filed - and the Company did carry short-term borrowings of Rs 62.52 lakhs (FY25) and Rs 43.13 lakhs (FY24) with cash-credit interest of Rs 8.07 and Rs 2.60 lakhs, so a facility against current assets did exist during the look-back.

Both Promoters were previously directors of three companies since struck off - Tazaamarket Private Limited, D Propshop India Private Limited and Nextbrands Marketing Solutions Private Limited (Risk Factor 30), all stated to be voluntary strike-offs.

The Company maintained NO insurance coverage at all during Fiscals 2023 and 2024; current cover of Rs 460.00 lakhs equals 0.26 times net tangible assets, and Risk Factor 23 contradicts itself by stating both that fire/burglary and Group Mediclaim cover was obtained and that the Company does not maintain any insurance policies in respect of its business and operations.

The Restated financials carry a caption error of consequence: 'Share Application Money' carries the values Rs 1,778.30 / 1,131.93 / 416.50 / 105.17 lakhs, which are in fact the Shareholders' Funds subtotals used as 'Shareholder's Equity' in the Note 27 Debt-Equity and Return-on-Equity ratios; read literally the line asserts Rs 1,778.30 lakhs of share application money pending allotment.

The EPS share-count basis is internally inconsistent: shares outstanding at year end were 0.10 lakh (FY2023) against a weighted average of 95.41 lakh used for EPS - roughly 954x - with no stated explanation of the retrospective bonus adjustment.

The Offer authorisation chain is out of sequence: the Board resolution under Section 62(1)(c) is dated July 10, 2026 and the enabling EGM special resolution July 13, 2026, both after the September 26, 2025 DRHP Board approval, the September 10, 2025 Selling Shareholder consents and the December 31, 2025 NSE in-principle approval.

Risk Factor text contains material carried over from an unrelated issuer: Risk Factor 53(h) refers to developments affecting 'India or its agrochemical industry' and Risk Factor 68 to the Company pursuing 'an acquisition driven growth strategy', neither of which matches the MICE / exhibition-stand business or is corroborated anywhere else in the document.

Execution footprint widened across every disclosed operational metric: total booths delivered globally 225 (FY23) to 256 to 381 to 432 (stub, stated CAGR 30.13% FY23-FY25); active subcontractors 22 to 29 to 36 to 53; international markets served 11 to 24; clients served 145 to 309; international clients from 20 to 69 (stated 245% growth over three years).

Export mix scaled from a near-nil base: international revenue Rs 15.91 lakhs (FY23) to Rs 35.32 (FY24) to Rs 331.76 (FY25) to Rs 767.05 lakhs (stub), i.e. 0.61% to 12.83% of revenue, with export sales stated to have risen 839.30% in Fiscal 2025 and 127.12% in the period ended February 28, 2026.

Disclosed order book of Rs 1,356.86 lakhs as at June 30, 2026 against Rs 741.38 lakhs as at February 28, 2026, spread over eleven customer industries.
